detail.longDescription: arXiv:2602.00272v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Safra's distributed termination detection algorithm employs a logical token ring structure within a distributed network; only passive nodes forward the token, and a counter in the token keeps track of the number of sent minus the number of received messages. We adapt this classic algorithm to make it fault-tolerant. The counter is split into counters per node, to discard counts from crashed nodes. If a node crashes, the token ring is restored locally and a backup token is sent. Nodes inform each other of detected crashes via the token. Our algorithm imposes no additional message overhead, tolerates any number of crashes as well as simultaneous crashes, and copes with crashes in a decentralized fashion. Correctness proofs are provided of both the original Safra's algorithm and its fault-tolerant variant, as well as a model checking analysis.
